messages:
david_support: Customer ACME reports SSO failures after an IdP cert rotation 10:02 UTC. Users see 403 / SAML Audience/Recipient mismatch. Tickets: #4365.

customer_acme_admin: We rotated our IdP certs last night (per vendor) and metadata URL now returns a new keychain. Logins stopped ~01:40 PT. No other config changes on our side.

maria_se: Can you paste the exact error? screenshot or error snippet helps.

customer_acme_admin: From the browser: "SAML response rejected: Recipient mismatch (expected https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs, got https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs/)" — note trailing slash. Happens for all users.

ken_devex: Interesting — trailing-slash mismatch. Our ACS canonicalization should accept both, but the assertion recipient is strict for some configs. Did you change the SP ACS in metadata?

customer_acme_admin: No, we did not touch SP metadata. Only IdP certs changed. The IdP metadata endpoint is https://idp.acme.com/metadata.xml and it now returns new <KeyDescriptor> entries.

idp-sync-bot: Automated metadata fetch at 02:05 UTC returned 200 with ETag: "W/"a1b2c3"". Stored checksum: md5=9f8b7c6a5. Current checksum: md5=bf34a1d9. Delta detected -> queued validation.

ops_oncall: Did the metadata fetcher validate the <AssertionConsumerService> entries? We had a bug where delta-checksum only looked at content-length and skipped full parsing — might have missed added trailing-slash rewrite rule upstream.

ken_devex: Repro steps I ran against their metadata:
```
curl -sS https://idp.acme.com/metadata.xml -o /tmp/metadata.xml
xmllint --noout /tmp/metadata.xml
grep -A2 AssertionConsumerService /tmp/metadata.xml
md5sum /tmp/metadata.xml
```
In their file the ACS location is listed as `https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs/` (with slash). Our stored SP entry expects no trailing slash.

maria_se: Root cause hypothesis: IdP cert rotation process also pushed a rewrite rule on their CDN that normalized ACS URLs with trailing slash. Our metadata delta-checksum pipeline flagged change but validation step skipped matching semantics (we compared host+path but ignored trailing slash normalization). So assertion got rejected.

david_support: Customer wants workaround ASAP. Any hotfix?

ken_devex: Fast mitigation options: 1) Update SP allowed ACS to accept trailing slash for that tenant (config change server-side) — low risk. 2) Ask customer to revert CDN rule or update their IdP metadata to canonical ACS. 3) Force metadata re-parse and full validation. I can push #1 as a temporary override.

maria_se: Can you confirm which tenants are affected? idp-sync-bot indicates only ACME-1 changed.

idp-sync-bot: Metadata change recorded for entityID 'https://idp.acme.com' -> tenant 'acme-1'. No other entities changed in last 24h.

ops_oncall: If we change SP ACS acceptance rules, need a quick rollback path and audit log. Also update canary to verify no open redirect/ACS confusion.

ken_devex: I'll open a canary change: toggle allow_trailing_slash:true for tenant acme-1 in SP config and reload SAML mapping. Command: `POST https://internal-console/api/tenants/acme-1/saml/override` payload `{ "allow_trailing_slash": true }` (ops will run).

maria_se: Also add a short-term validation rule to metadata pipeline: treat trailing slash as equivalent when comparing ACS locations. We'll add test coverage.

david_support: Executed workaround at 10:24 UTC. Customer says SSO works for a subset of users now, most can sign in. Monitoring showing 200s.

customer_acme_admin: Login success confirmed for 90% of users. Thanks, please advise next steps for permanent fix.

ken_devex: Next steps: 1) schedule a postmortem with ACME to understand why CDN added rewrite during cert rotation. 2) Long-term: make metadata delta check canonicalize ACS URLs before checksum. 3) Add audit event when we auto-accept structural ACS changes.

maria_se: I'll draft the RCA. Initial cause: IdP cert rotation + CDN rewrite caused metadata semantics change; our delta-checksum/validation pipeline missed normalized path differences.

david_support: Closing loop with customer, will attach logs & timeline. Thanks team. :tada:
